rules.appliesWhen: Investigating an incorrect implementation or human correction
rules.instruction: Diagnose missing knowledge, unapplied guidance, ambiguous/new requirements or tooling failure. Reuse/clarify rules or improve workflow/automation rather than append a paraphrase per correction.
rules.reason: More instructions do not cure failures to apply existing knowledge.

rules.appliesWhen: Updating accumulated implementation experience
rules.instruction: Keep actionable scoped rules, brief reasons and useful examples. Merge duplicates, explicitly replace superseded policy, and retain exceptions and applicable experience. Check analogous/excluded cases for nontrivial generalizations; simple preferences need no expensive blind ceremony.
rules.reason: A coherent current guide prevents mistakes better than an accumulating history.

rules.appliesWhen: Assessing whether accumulated experience improves quality
rules.instruction: Compare recurring mistakes, substantive user corrections, initial-review defects and false alarms across comparable tasks. Distinguish first-implementation quality from review-assisted delivery; verification or a larger catalog is not measured improvement.
rules.reason: The goal is fewer wrong implementations and user corrections, not an audit trail.

rules.appliesWhen: Changing files consumed by a running plugin or hook
rules.instruction: Stage the new format separately, make the consumer compatible first, and establish reload behavior before switching live data. Preserve a compatible bridge for already-loaded hooks and verify migration completeness before retiring the old format.
rules.reason: A live hook can reject new data before the updated loader has been activated.

rules.appliesWhen: Production mappings and third-party reference data
rules.instruction: Use independent representative expected values, including an excluded value for filtered data. Do not reproduce production registry/filtering logic or maintain exhaustive provider lists unless exhaustive membership is the contract.
rules.reason: Mirroring implementation can reproduce its defect; exhaustive external fixtures add maintenance.

rules.appliesWhen: Adding GraphQL API tests
rules.instruction: When adding API tests, compare neighboring tests and preserve their authorization/business-flow nesting conventions. Organize GraphQL tests by mutation and by reasonable query hierarchy level rather than one broad API test class.
rules.reason: Consistent boundaries expose missing business and authorization scenarios.

rules.appliesWhen: Testing optional API input
rules.instruction: Model nullable optional API input as null and test an actual empty string separately; never equate null with omission of a wire input unless the request construction proves omission.
rules.reason: Null, empty and omitted wire fields have different semantics.

rules.appliesWhen: Assigning reusable component and consuming-page interaction coverage
rules.instruction: Keep reusable interaction-state coverage in component-specific Kotlin full-stack tests, including overview-filter helpers rather than new frontend helper unit tests. Keep page business conditions, validation and loading in existing page tests without component-test duplication. Moving one component's coverage does not ban unrelated tests/frameworks.
rules.reason: Coverage should follow behavior ownership without duplicating expensive workflows.

rules.appliesWhen: Submissions with transient notifications and persistent field errors
rules.instruction: For submissions producing transient notifications and persistent field errors, assert the notification first without waiting for it to disappear.
rules.reason: Checking persistent state first can miss a transient notification.

rules.appliesWhen: Input changes that invalidate dependent values and start async work
rules.instruction: On dependent-input changes, reset at transition start; use finally only for local cleanup, let shared error handling surface failures, and guard stale asynchronous results.
rules.reason: Late responses or old selections can overwrite current input state.

rules.appliesWhen: Implementing form components
rules.instruction: Form components must use the standard SaFormItemInternal v-model binding and local value state instead of casting/indexing injected form values.
rules.reason: Standard binding preserves the form contract and type safety.

rules.appliesWhen: Explaining a questioned test-selector change
rules.instruction: When a test-selector change is questioned, provide its concrete DOM/rendering rationale in the review report; add source comments only when the code itself needs non-obvious durable explanation.
rules.reason: A report explanation and a source comment serve different purposes.

rules.appliesWhen: Committing implementation or feedback corrections
rules.instruction: Commit completed relevant turns separately by default, including prior progress before feedback. Explicit no-commit instructions override that default and are not a workflow defect. Scoped authorization covers only that scope, not later corrections or publication.
rules.reason: Workflow defaults must respect explicit user control.

rules.appliesWhen: Resuming review after human feedback
rules.instruction: Each distinct feedback turn has up to two review rounds with fresh round, repair, time and cost limits. Refresh knowledge and review cumulative changes against the original base, including analogous earlier-turn issues. Preserve cumulative usage and prior state. Whitespace-equivalent duplicate feedback and ordinary continuation never reset limits.
rules.reason: Distinct feedback needs current review without evading limits through duplicate requests.

rules.appliesWhen: Responding to human corrections or preferences
rules.instruction: Investigate every item, including new preferences. Preserve exact comments and stable refs across follow-ups; label summaries and carry unresolved items forward. Ask with evidence and options about genuine conflicts rather than dismissing feedback. Report ref, file:line, initial comment, correction and active rule/remedy or unresolved status.
rules.reason: Partial handling leaves known mistakes unresolved.

rules.appliesWhen: Explaining behavior or learning from corrections
rules.instruction: State evidence precisely; distinguish documentation from reported rationale and null from omitted input. Keep defaults subject to explicit overrides. Use neutral anonymous-login copy.
rules.reason: Unsupported diagnoses produce unreliable prevention.

rules.appliesWhen: Starting implementation or publishing learned guidance
rules.instruction: Apply the complete active catalog before coding; identify relevant approach constraints. Inject every distilled rule: never silently truncate or leave accepted guidance undeployed. Validate and size-check the same active projection. Feedback reports identify active rule IDs and catalog path; verification is not measured improvement.
rules.reason: Prevention before coding is stronger than catching the same defect during review.

rules.appliesWhen: API writes whose values depend on another field, including residency/currency
rules.instruction: Enforce cross-field constraints on the server and add negative API tests proving rejected input leaves persistence unchanged. Preserve authorization and optimistic-version precedence before edit validation and permit repairs of legacy inconsistent records.
rules.reason: Direct API callers bypass UI filtering.

rules.appliesWhen: Defining application or integration configuration
rules.instruction: Use documented typed @ConfigurationProperties rooted under sa, with provider settings under sa.integrations.<provider>. Do not add ad-hoc @Value properties.
rules.reason: Typed domain-owned configuration keeps settings consistent.

rules.appliesWhen: Providers with multiple API versions
rules.instruction: Keep third-party API origins version-neutral when multiple provider API versions must coexist; select the supported version explicitly per endpoint.
rules.reason: A version embedded in the origin prevents mixed-version endpoints.

rules.appliesWhen: Exposing workspace-owned integration metadata in GraphQL
rules.instruction: Nest metadata under Workspace.integrations.<provider>.<data>, not standalone status/provider root queries. Name the API and root DTO documentation after the provider-neutral integrations domain; reserve provider names for provider-scoped types. Describe third-party IDs as opaque unless clients should interpret them.
rules.reason: Workspace ownership and extensible naming prevent flat first-provider-specific APIs.

rules.appliesWhen: Mapping expected business failures, isolating scheduled batch items, or sharing integration fetching across scheduled and async entry points
rules.instruction: Use @BusinessError and dedicated exceptions for expected failures; business operations catch only specific locally actionable failures. Scheduled per-item orchestration may catch Exception after specific handlers, never JVM Errors or the whole batch. Preserve failed-item rollback and continuation; log unexpected failures at ERROR with the complete throwable and integration/item context, not just its message/class. Keep provider diagnostics bounded and credential-redacted and public errors sanitized. For fetching shared by scheduled/async callers, isolate in the common single-integration service operation outside its transaction, giving both callers rollback and diagnostics.
rules.reason: Per-item isolation protects unrelated work; a shared service boundary also protects async callers while retaining complete troubleshooting evidence.

rules.appliesWhen: Exhausting automated review rounds
rules.instruction: A two-round review limit caps automated review, not delivery work: after exhaustion, finish required implementation and validation, report the exhausted limit, receipt status, and remaining issues, and seek direction only for genuine ambiguity or external blockers.
rules.reason: A review budget caps automation, not delivery of required fixes.

rules.appliesWhen: Implementing provider clients and configuration
rules.instruction: Keep provider clients internal to their business integration service; APIs depend only on that service. Place provider-specific client/configuration implementation with its owning business integration when it is not shared infrastructure.
rules.reason: The owning service prevents provider details leaking into APIs.

rules.appliesWhen: Designing page and menu full-stack tests
rules.instruction: Do not maintain UI tests for unsupported direct routes when dedicated menu and API authorization coverage own those concerns. Keep navigation clicks in dedicated menu tests; page tests should open their target pages directly.
rules.reason: Repeated navigation obscures the page business workflow.

rules.appliesWhen: Validating static integration cards and instructional content
rules.instruction: Use rendering reports for static integration-card and instructional content; retain source assertions for interactive and stateful behavior only.
rules.reason: Rendering review avoids assertions duplicating static copy.

rules.appliesWhen: Adding stubs, page objects, component wrappers and utilities
rules.instruction: Name test stubbing helpers as actions; avoid getter-like names for setup operations. Keep one-page wrappers in their page object and shared components in reusable infrastructure. Generic-component DOM structure, locator counts and internal class/icon checks belong to that component's wrapper; page objects delegate through typed methods and composed wrappers. Preserve unrelated generic APIs and callers. Add helpers beside equivalent existing utilities rather than creating parallel utility files.
rules.reason: Clear ownership prevents generic DOM leakage and parallel utility hierarchies.

rules.appliesWhen: User-directed removal of unnecessary tests
rules.instruction: Remove user-rejected tests, not required production safety. Mobile support and mobile-only code/tests are out of scope unless requested.
rules.reason: Removing redundant coverage does not revoke production requirements.

rules.appliesWhen: Testing internal provider clients
rules.instruction: Test internal provider clients through their owning service and a WireMock server, not through direct client test classes.
rules.reason: Service boundaries cover observable integration behavior.

rules.appliesWhen: Adding client-side access gates
rules.instruction: Do not add unexplained client-side access gates where server authorization is the authoritative boundary.
rules.reason: UI gating is not authorization.

rules.appliesWhen: Non-reused page behavior such as an integration wizard
rules.instruction: Keep single-use behavior and styles in the owning Vue page/component; do not retain a pass-through wrapper unless it has reusable or independent value. Use shared styles only when genuinely shared.
rules.reason: Pass-through layers and scattered styles make behavior harder to follow.

rules.appliesWhen: GraphQL fields requiring additional computation or database access
rules.instruction: Defer work to the selected resolver boundary. When sibling metadata fields share one backing record, load it once with authorization in their nearest selected parent resolver and derive siblings from that object. Keep outer namespace construction lightweight and independently expensive children lazy.
rules.reason: Field laziness must not multiply shared reads or eagerly resolve unselected providers.

rules.appliesWhen: Implementing fixed-workspace pages
rules.instruction: Do not subscribe fixed-workspace page views to workspace-change events intended for persistent application chrome; avoid wrappers whose only purpose is that redundant lifecycle.
rules.reason: Redundant subscriptions introduce stale-state paths.

rules.appliesWhen: Considering follow-up database migrations
rules.instruction: Before adding a follow-up migration for unmerged work, establish the predecessor migration's merge/release status; amend the unmerged migration when appropriate instead of creating a redundant successor.
rules.reason: Unreleased migrations can often be corrected directly.

rules.appliesWhen: Setting up backend and full-stack tests
rules.instruction: Set up through real services and persistence-backed preconditions/lazyPreconditions factories, never aggregateTemplate. Name multiple arguments; default unrelated values. Mock only unavoidable external boundaries; prefer persistence over repository mocks/spies. Each distinct feedback turn must audit cumulative branch changes for analogous issues; without this audit no clean receipt.
rules.reason: Realistic setup exercises application boundaries instead of implementation details.

rules.appliesWhen: Testing GraphQL lazy fields
rules.instruction: Do not add tests for GraphQL framework-guaranteed field laziness; test application behavior and retain lazy resolver structure where required.
rules.reason: Framework-mechanics tests add coupling without application coverage.

rules.appliesWhen: Asserting and interacting with dynamic repeated UI items
rules.instruction: For dynamic repeated UI items, page objects must expose retrying typed snapshots and tests must assert exact ordered collections so unexpected items fail the assertion. After exhaustive collection assertions, identify an item by one stable field; first assert exactly one typed item matches it, then assert exactly one UI locator and interact.
rules.reason: Partial assertions and first-match selection hide unexpected or duplicate items.

rules.appliesWhen: Handling GraphQL/API errors in pages
rules.instruction: Rely on the global handler for generic GraphQL/API failures; add page-local handling only for business errors whose recovery or presentation is page-specific.
rules.reason: Duplicate handlers create inconsistent or suppressed feedback.

rules.appliesWhen: Testing successful credential-backed setup
rules.instruction: A successful credential-backed setup flow must assert every required persisted setting, including the credential where the test fixture can safely inspect it. Merge overlapping full-stack success scenarios when identical provider mocking and setup flow differ only in additional assertions; retain distinct workflows only for independently meaningful behavior.
rules.reason: UI success can hide incomplete persistence; overlapping journeys waste validation time.

rules.appliesWhen: Ordinary page-local Vue async flows
rules.instruction: Do not add unmount/disposal guards to ordinary page-local Vue async flows unless a concrete lifecycle requirement demonstrates that framework lifecycle handling is insufficient; keep ordinary error handling intact.
rules.reason: Speculative lifecycle machinery adds complexity; dependent-input races remain a distinct concern.

rules.appliesWhen: Representing multi-step UI state, especially object-defined wizard consumers
rules.instruction: Use semantic named constants rather than raw numeric indices, preserving library index conventions. For object-defined wizard pages, group step IDs in one semantic steps object and derive the ID type from it.
rules.reason: A consistent semantic step model improves readability and prevents separately maintained ID types.

rules.appliesWhen: Diagnosing credential-backed provider setup
rules.instruction: For credential-backed third-party setup, provide bounded credential-redacted server diagnostics identifying the endpoint and either HTTP/provider failure response, empty or malformed response, or transport no-response cause; retain sanitized public business errors.
rules.reason: Useful diagnostics must locate failures without disclosing credentials.

rules.appliesWhen: Testing integration diagnostics
rules.instruction: Do not add tests that assert logging or log output. Retain production bounded credential-redacted diagnostics where required, and test observable service behavior rather than diagnostic log emission.
rules.reason: Tests should cover service behavior rather than diagnostic emission.

rules.appliesWhen: Changing Wise setup status presentation
rules.instruction: Wizard loading status panels must use the same centered result layout as completed success panels; inspect rendered loading states as well as completed states when changing wizard status presentation.
rules.reason: Loading and completed states need visual consistency and accessible announcements.

rules.appliesWhen: Naming GraphQL operations and exposed fields
rules.instruction: Use names that describe the observable domain action and state, not incidental internal steps or UI-local interaction terms; preserve UI vocabulary inside UI-only models.
rules.reason: API names are long-lived client contracts and should not misstate credential or persistence behavior.

rules.appliesWhen: Writing Kotlin calls or constructors with more than one supplied argument
rules.instruction: Use named arguments for every supplied argument, except Java calls, individual vararg elements and genuine DSL builder methods such as JSON put/putJsonArray, which retain idiomatic positional arguments and trailing lambdas. Ordinary service, factory and constructor calls still require named arguments inside DSL receivers.
rules.reason: Names clarify ordinary multi-value calls; DSL builders retain their idiomatic structure.

rules.appliesWhen: Documenting optional GraphQL credential or similarly stateful inputs
rules.instruction: Document supplied, null, omitted, empty, and blank semantics where applicable, including the effective value and whether it is persisted, replaced, or retained.
rules.reason: Generated schema documentation is the client-facing contract for wire-input semantics.

rules.appliesWhen: A test contains independently meaningful create, update, replacement, deletion, rejection or query contracts, including pagination, isolation and optional filter dimensions
rules.instruction: Split independent workflows or query contracts into separate tests with their own relevant preconditions and outcome assertions. Retain a compact parameterized or table-driven test for variants sharing one setup boundary and observable outcome.
rules.reason: Independent contracts need isolated failure signals; equivalent boundary variants do not.

rules.appliesWhen: Defining or mapping the provider-neutral AccountStatementRecord model
rules.instruction: Use IntegrationProvider for supported providers and one StatementType enum containing DEBIT, CREDIT, CONVERSION and OTHER, with unsupported activities mapped to OTHER. Preserve structured monetary conversion data, consolidate supplementary text into labeled additionalData, and keep provider-specific profile context and parsing inside adapters.
rules.reason: Copying provider fields into generic persistence leaks provider concepts and duplicates classification.

rules.appliesWhen: Mapping and persisting the primary statement transaction amount
rules.instruction: Document and store an absolute, nonnegative minor-unit magnitude; normalize negative provider amounts with checked arithmetic and reject unrepresentable magnitudes. Enforce the invariant in the entity and database and cover debit, credit, conversion, unknown activity and minimum-long input. Do not apply this magnitude rule to signed running balances.
rules.reason: Unchecked absolute-value conversion can overflow and signed amounts contradict the model contract.

rules.appliesWhen: Statement-record deduplication and provider-reference normalization
rules.instruction: Use integrationId, accountId and externalId consistently for lookup and database uniqueness. Adapters must produce opaque external IDs unique within that integration/account, encoding provider-specific distinctions when needed to preserve refunds or separate statement entries; do not add currency, direction or provider profile columns to the generic identity.
rules.reason: Raw provider references may collide, while provider-specific lookup columns undermine the generic identity contract.

rules.appliesWhen: Adding or changing database migrations
rules.instruction: Keep application defaults explicit rather than retaining database column defaults. For existing records, either use a temporary default and drop it after backfill or add nullable, update, then set not null. Check cumulative migration changes for retained defaults and respect released-migration immutability.
rules.reason: Persistent database defaults hide write behavior from application code.

rules.appliesWhen: Asserting complete persisted-entity mappings
rules.instruction: Use shouldBeEntityWithFields with an independently specified expected entity, including meaningful default-valued fields, instead of fragmented property assertions. Keep focused assertions for tests whose contract concerns only selected fields.
rules.reason: Full-entity expectations expose missing or unexpectedly populated mapped fields.

rules.appliesWhen: Implementing Spring integration fetching shared by periodic scheduling and enabled-save background dispatch
rules.instruction: Own batch scheduling, single-integration async dispatch and guarded fetching in the fetch service: no pass-through jobs/triggers or single-item dispatch through batch jobs. After enabled-save commit, invoke its proxied @Async method directly with async support enabled; no manual executor or single-consumer event bridge. Never dispatch disabled, rejected or rolled-back saves; keep fetch transactions independent.
rules.reason: One owner avoids redundant orchestration while preserving real asynchronous execution and commit ordering.

rules.appliesWhen: Implementing or changing scheduled and asynchronous account-statement fetching
rules.instruction: In the owning fetch service, log scheduled-run, integration and account starts/ends with safe IDs, explicit outcomes and durations; include selected/processed integration counts, account intervals, retrieved records and completed windows. Per-window counts belong at DEBUG. Distinguish retrieval from persistence: report import/duplicate success only after commit, never for failed/rolled-back work. Preserve credential redaction, exception isolation and no-log-assertion policies.
rules.reason: Lifecycle gaps obscure stalled work, while precommit success statistics misrepresent rolled-back imports.

rules.appliesWhen: Complex inline TypeScript union/intersection types with semantically distinct alternatives
rules.instruction: Extract meaningful named alternatives and shared options so the composite type reads in domain terms. Do not extract every simple inline type.
rules.reason: Anonymous compound alternatives obscure the contract.

rules.appliesWhen: Implementing or consuming the shared object-defined wizard
rules.instruction: Navigate only through bottom-bar buttons; titles are noninteractive and content controls selection-only. Derive adjacent actions from step order; omit only first Back/last Next and disable blocked actions. Pages supply completion facts and one top-level loading value; the wizard derives statuses and locks actions during loading/pending callbacks. Retain page validity and service re-entry guards.
rules.reason: Central ownership prevents inconsistent navigation and repeated presentation or busy-state logic.

rules.appliesWhen: Applying an application-wide visual theme
rules.instruction: Inventory all shared component styles, library semantic palettes and page overrides; use centralized tokens across surfaces and interaction states, not only showcase pages. Preserve behavior, semantic distinctions, simplified variants, disabled actions and third-party brands.
rules.reason: Global token changes alone leave local overrides and library states visually inconsistent.

rules.appliesWhen: Choosing the account-statements navigation icon
rules.instruction: Use the dedicated account-statements icon, not the reporting icon.
rules.reason: Account statements and reporting are distinct navigation destinations.

rules.appliesWhen: Filtering timestamped records by browser-local calendar dates; excludes date-only domain fields and explicitly specified non-browser timezone contracts
rules.instruction: Send timestamp bounds to the API: inclusive browser-local midnight at the selected start and exclusive local midnight after the selected end. Advance by calendar date, not a fixed 24-hour duration, and cover boundary inclusion/exclusion on both 23-hour and 25-hour DST days.
rules.reason: UTC date boundaries and fixed-day durations select the wrong records around timezone offsets and DST.

rules.appliesWhen: Presenting account-statement transaction details
rules.instruction: Do not display internal integration IDs or internal statement-record IDs in the details list. Retain identifiers internally where needed, and preserve meaningful provider account and external transaction references.
rules.reason: Internal persistence identifiers add noise without helping users interpret transactions.

rules.appliesWhen: Rendering account-statement transaction types or implementing an explicitly requested iconless status badge; excludes intentionally simplified text labels
rules.instruction: Use SaStatusLabel with hide-icon and without simplified for iconless badges. Preserve semantic status mappings and shared component behavior rather than introducing custom badge styles.
rules.reason: Icon visibility and badge styling are independent props; simplified removes the badge background.

rules.appliesWhen: Testing API authorization with ownership, shared access or workspace-token boundaries
rules.instruction: Enumerate applicable actors from source authorization boundaries: owner, anonymous, administrator, unrelated user, saved-share user, matching/unrelated workspace tokens and expired/revoked tokens where supported. Assert actual returned data for allowed actors and source-derived error contracts for rejected actors; do not assume administrator access or a universal rejection code.
rules.reason: Role-only coverage misses sharing and token boundaries and can encode incorrect rejection semantics.

rules.appliesWhen: Testing API search across multiple supported fields
rules.instruction: Explicitly enumerate every supported field in parameterized cases with independently specified exact expected matches. Use discriminating same-scope records and mixed-case substrings or IDs as applicable; respect domain constraints when fields necessarily match multiple records rather than inventing unsupported values. Cover literal wildcard/escape characters, unmatched input and applicable null/empty/blank contracts separately.
rules.reason: Sparse or implementation-derived cases can miss omitted fields and accidental matches.

rules.appliesWhen: Implementing, documenting or testing account-statement free-text search; excludes unrelated entity search contracts
rules.instruction: Search only accountId, externalId, type, partyName and additionalData. Exclude id, integrationId, provider and all currency columns, not occurrences of their values inside searchable text. Preserve dedicated providerIn filtering, workspace authorization and persistence/pagination identifiers. Keep schema documentation and generated artifacts aligned. Independently enumerate the five included fields in positive parameterized API cases with contrasting same-workspace records. Do not add regression tests asserting excluded-column membership; manually review the production allowlist instead. Audit cumulative statement query tests/docs for obsolete membership expectations. Preserve unrelated wildcard/escape, unmatched and optional-input tests.
rules.reason: Explicit search membership keeps results relevant; scoped user-directed test removal must not weaken production exclusions or unrelated coverage.

rules.appliesWhen: Preparing or conducting source reviews, compliance reviews or feedback audits involving generated artifacts
rules.instruction: Exclude artifacts marked linguist-generated in Git attributes from review snapshots, diffs, source packets and audits before content/size checks. Review authored sources, generator/verification definitions and attribute changes instead. Generated-output verification remains the primary agent's build/CI responsibility; preserve secret-path safeguards before exclusion.
rules.reason: Reviewing generated output duplicates automated verification and can block review of authored changes.
